newsitem.title: USA: Argentina to weigh options on Yacyreta if blocked.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to weigh options on Yacyreta if blocked.

text.p: Argentina's government will look for alternative ways of privatizing the $8.5 billion Yacyreta hydroelectric dam project if parliament blocks it, though there is no intention of issuing a decree to bypass the legislature, according to a government secretary.

"There is no intention of using decree power because it is not necessary and also because the decision could be taken by the bi-national commission (between Argentina and Paraguay)," said Alfredo Mirkin, Argentina's secretary of energy and ports, speaking at a seminar in New York sponsored by the Council of the Americas on investment prospects in Argentina's energy sector.

A protocol signed by Argentine President Carlos Menem and his Paraguayan counterpart Juan Carlos Wasmosy last year set a deadline of April 30 for both parliaments to approve the privatization of the dam.

"If it is not approved, we would have to start to analyse with Paraguay the alternatives that would permit a continuation of the project...(But) the Argentine government would not continue to finance the project from the treasury or to guarantee loans," said Mirkin.
The secretary said specific alternatives have not yet been fully worked out, though some form of tender might be considered.
Mirkin said that a tender, for example, might be based on payment in electricity and the entity bidding for the lowest payback in power wins.
Mirkin estimated that the amount needed to complete the project, not including current environmental works under way, is around $800 million.
((-- Patricia Garip-Bertuol, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620))
